# ROCTECH Case Knowledge Base

Real customer cases, application solutions, and hard selling points for ROCTECH (Roctech Machinery Co., Ltd) CNC routers and ROCLAS fibre lasers. Compiled from roc-tech.com and the local "若泰机器资料" archive. Oct 2026.

This is a working knowledge base, not a brochure. It pulls together the things sales and support actually need: who the customers are, what machine they bought, what problem they had, and what changed after. The 12 customer cases are kept in their original wording, with a short ROCTECH note added to each. The rest is arranged so you can find a proof point fast.

## What's inside

- [Company Profile](company-profile.md) — What ROCTECH makes, certifications, contact
- [Product & Solution Map](product-solutions.md) — 13 product lines mapped to real models
- [Industry Solutions](application-industries.md) — 8 industries, each tied to a real case

- [Sources & Gaps](data-sources-scope.md) — Where the data came from, what's missing

## The numbers at a glance

### 15 years

Building CNC routers and lasers. Certified to ISO 9001 (2018) and CE (2014).

### 12 countries

Documented customer cases across 4 continents: woodworking, plastics, and metal lasers.

### 10 years

Longest running machine in the case files (Romania, 2016). Still in daily use.

### ~80%

Polishing work cut when a Malaysian shop dropped plasma for a ROCTECH laser.

# Company Profile

ROCTECH (Roctech Machinery Co., Ltd) — CNC routers and fibre lasers, made in Jinan, China. Lasers sell under the ROCLAS name.

ROCTECH builds CNC routers and fibre laser cutting machines, and has done for 15 years. They're not the biggest name in the category, but they ship to 100+ countries and a fair number of their customers come back and buy again. The facts below are the ones worth leading with when someone asks "who are these guys?"

**Two brands, one company**

**ROCTECH** and **ROCLAS** are two brands of the same manufacturer — Jinan Ruotai CNC Technology Co., Ltd. (若泰数控), headquartered in Jinan, China.

**ROCTECH** is the main brand for CNC routers and machining centers: woodworking routers, ATC nesting machines, edge banders, panel drills, and 4-/5-axis stone, foam and mold machines.

**ROCLAS** is the sub-brand for fibre laser cutting machines — sheet, tube, and combined sheet-and-tube models.

That is why some cases here carry the ROCTECH name and others ROCLAS: same manufacturer, two product-line brands.

### Who they are

**Name**: Roctech Machinery Co., Ltd (Chinese: 济南若泰数控科技有限公司)

**What**: CNC routers + fibre laser machines, R&D / build / export

**Base**: Jinan, Shandong (HQ + Qihe factory), Hong Kong office

**Experience**: 15 years in CNC routers

**Patents**: 50+ held, about 10 new each year

**R &D**: 15-person team, most with 15+ years in the trade

**Reach**: Exports to 100+ countries

### Certifications

`ISO 9001` `CE` `FDA (lasers)` `UL` `PDL` `RoHS`

Certification years from local records: **CE in 2014** , **ISO 9001 in 2018** — that's what opened the export market for them.

Cert numbers — ISO 9001: 31623Q10581R1S · CE: ICR/VC/HM2403124 · FDA Laser: 2521816-000 / 2520443-000

### What they're known for

• **Accuracy:** mid-range routers quoted at 0.01 mm positioning / 0.005 mm repeat; 5-axis verified at 0.01 mm under a live 18,000 rpm spindle load.

• **Holding up:** one customer ran a machine 10 hrs/day, 6 days/week for 7+ years and only ever replaced a $200 belt.

• **Saving material:** a cabinet shop dropped scrap from 18% to 7%.

• **Lower running cost:** roughly 15–20% less power than comparable machines.

• **Support:** 1 year of free spare parts, free first-year training, 2-year warranty on core parts, EU/US spare-parts stock.

### Get in touch

**Phone**: +86 531-86085880

**Email**: info@roc-tech.com · support@roc-tech.com

**WhatsApp**: +86 13705409964

**Sales**: Dedicated inboxes for Chinese / Russian / Spanish / Arabic / Portuguese

**One line to remember:** ROCTECH isn't selling the cheapest machine on the page. They're selling a machine that's still cutting a decade later, backed by a team that picks up the phone. That's the pitch the case files back up.

Sources: roc-tech.com (about-us, contact-us, faq) and local 若泰机器资料 (roctech_faqs, certification records).

# Product & Solution Map

Every product line ROCTECH builds, the models customers actually received, and what each one is for. Laser models carry the ROCLAS name.

This table is built from two sources: the product pages on roc-tech.com, and the actual machine models that show up in the 12 customer cases. When a model has been shipped to a real customer, we say so — that's more useful than a catalogue number.

Product line| Models seen in the field| What it does| Typical use
---|---|---|---
Woodworking ATC router| RC1325S-ATC, RC1530S-ATC (1500×3000)| 8–24 tool automatic changer + vacuum table| Custom furniture, signs, carving
Cabinet / panel line| RCA1224 nesting centre, RCE edge bander, 5/6-side drill| Nesting + edge banding + drilling in one flow| Whole-house custom, kitchen cabinets
5-axis machining centre| RCF1325 / 1838 / 2040 / 2560| ±110° A-axis + 360° C-axis, OSAI control| Moulds, curved wood, foam, stone
HDPE / plastic line| HDPE processing line (Chile case)| Chain feed + cleaning system, steady run| Plastic sheet processing
Fibre laser (flat)| RCL3015-3000W / 2000W / Eco, RC3015L (open)| 3000W: 10 mm CS / 6 mm SS / 4 mm AL; ±0.03 mm| Sheet metal, elevator, industrial
Fibre laser (high power)| 6000W (MAX/Raycus/IPG), up to 10–20 kW| Cuts carbon steel to ~25 mm| Medium/thick plate, volume
Sheet-and-tube laser| RC3015T / 3015 combo (UK/Russia/Spain)| One machine for sheet and tube, 5–10 min swap| Steel structure, craft metal, mixed jobs
Exchange-table / large laser| RCL2040-EX-3K (2000×4000 shuttle)| Load/unload overlaps cutting, 80,000 mm/min rapid| High-volume metal work
Dedicated tube laser| RCL2400-3000W tube cutter| Round/square tube specialist (Spain two-line setup)| Railings, tube parts
Laser weld / clean / CO₂| Laser welding / cleaning / CO₂| Handheld weld, surface cleaning| Welding, rust removal
Sign / mould / 4-axis| Sign Makers line, Big CNC for Molds (EPS), 4-axis| Acrylic letters, foam moulds, rotary parts| Advertising, moulds, cylinders

**Read this before quoting:** The RCL / RC / ROCLAS codes are real shipped models. Power, price, and cutting thickness are indicative from the cases and articles — always confirm the exact spec with ROCTECH before you put a number in front of a customer.

Sources: roc-tech.com product centre + customer case files (RCL/RC are actually shipped models).

# Industry Solutions

Eight materials and industries ROCTECH handles, each one tied to a customer who actually did it.

Most "solutions" pages are wish lists. This one isn't — every card below points to a real case in the [Customer Cases](cases/) section. If you're talking to a shop in that industry, you've got a proof point ready.

### Panel furniture / cabinets

Nesting centre → edge bander → 6-side drill as one line. The proof: a cabinet shop cut scrap from 18% to 7%, and ROCTECH wrote up a real visit to a shop that switched to their centre.

[See cases →](cases/)

### Solid wood / curved parts

5-axis RCF series machines chair backs and bent legs in one setup. The proof: a Romanian workshop has run ROCTECH woodworking machines for 10 years on carved pavilions and lattice work.

[Romania case →](cases/romania.md)

### Moulds / foam

RCF 5-axis plus the Big CNC for Molds (EPS) line. Car, aerospace, and sculpture foam moulds.

### Stone carving

Tiered setup from entry 3-axis to 5-axis. The hard parts are sealed rails, coolant, and spindle cooling — buy a stone machine, not a wood router with a stone bit.

### Signs / advertising

CNC Router for Sign Makers line; acrylic and PVC letters. The proof: a US makerspace runs an RC1530S-ATC doing sign engraving day in, day out.

[USA case →](cases/usa-reno.md)

### Metal / aluminium

Fibre lasers — flat, tube, sheet-and-tube, high power — plus CNC. The proof: eight laser cases across Malaysia, Spain, Italy, Mexico and more.

[Laser cases →](cases/)

### Education / makerspaces

RC series with DSP controller, no PC needed. The proof: the Reno makerspace's ROCTECH has survived years of different operators.

[USA case →](cases/usa-reno.md)

### Plastics / HDPE

HDPE line with chain feed and cleaning system. The proof: Guillermo in Chile runs one steadily and is coming back for loading/unloading systems.

[Chile case →](cases/chile.md)

Sources: roc-tech.com industry articles (newslist/1108, 1109, 1110) + the 12 customer cases.

# Selling Points & Real Buying Scenarios

The numbers ROCTECH customers actually quote, plus the buying questions that come up most.

This page is for the conversation, not the catalogue. The figures below come from ROCTECH's own FAQ records and from the customer cases. Lead with the one that fits the customer in front of you.

## The numbers that close deals

### Accuracy

Mid-range routers quoted at 0.01 mm positioning, 0.005 mm repeat. The 5-axis is verified at 0.01 mm with the spindle spinning at 18,000 rpm under load — not measured while it's parked, which is how a lot of specs get fudged.

### Reliability

One customer ran a machine 10 hrs/day, 6 days/week for 7+ years and only ever replaced a $200 belt. ROCTECH backs it with 1 year of free parts, free first-year training, and 2-year warranty on core parts.

### Material savings

A cabinet shop took scrap from 18% down to 7% — about 61% less waste. At 40 sheets a week at $65 a sheet, that's roughly $16,900 a year back in material.

### Power & hidden cost

About 15-20% less power than comparable machines. CAM software alone runs $5k-15k a year, so bundle a spare-parts package at purchase and skip the panic later.

### Compliance you can show

CE (2014) and ISO 9001 (2018). ROCTECH supplies third-party load-accuracy reports, pre-ship test reports, and video factory tours so a buyer can verify before paying.

### Industry 4.0, lightly

Newer machines ship with vibration and temperature sensors, optional remote monitoring, and early warnings on spindle heat or axis vibration. Useful, not gimmicky.

## Real buying scenarios (from the FAQ)

These are actual questions people asked ROCTECH, with the answer that went out. Good for handling the same objection when it shows up again.

### Soft-metal memorial plaque

4"×6" half-inch brass: at least 300W and a rigid Z-axis. RC0609 with a 3.0 kW HSD spindle (~$3,500+). Brass engraving uses a 30-60° V-bit, 0.1-0.3 mm deep, with a thin WD-40 mist.

### High-school robotics team — aluminium

At least 1.5 kW, ball screw, 50 kg+ frame. RC0609 (3.0-6.5 kW, ~1450 kg) can qualify for STEM grants up to $5,000.

### Campus makerspace, 4×8

RC1325 + DSP controller + 3.0 kW HSD + Yaskawa + vacuum table + full enclosure. The DSP controller runs without a PC, which is the most stable setup for mixed operators.

### Hobbyist / high-accuracy / rigid

The rest of the FAQ covers the entry buyer (~$1k), tiny-bit work (<$3.5k), sub-$1.2k rigid frames, 4×8 wood, AvidCNC vs build-your-own, the $10-15k tier, and how to avoid eBay traps. Titles only here — see roc-tech.com/faq for the full answers.

**Honest gap:** The official FAQ has 26 questions; only 10 are captured in the local records (IDs 766-775). The numbers above are solid; the missing 16 are just not in this archive yet.

Sources: roc-tech.com/faq + local roctech_faqs record. Accuracy figures carry a note — the official site lists ±0.05 mm for the RCF1325, while the FAQ claims 0.01 mm. Confirm per model.

# Technical Notes

The engineering points that actually come up when someone's spec'ing a machine. Short and to the point.

### Vacuum hold-down

Zoned, double-layer tables hold a tiny part and a full sheet on the same bed without losing vacuum. Matters more than people think once nesting gets tight.

### Drilling built in

Putting the drill bank inside the cutting cycle, plus a 6-side drill for one-setup holes, kills a whole class of assembly errors. That's how the cabinet line hits its material savings.

### Software continuity

Nesting software talking straight to the controller, no hand-typed G-code in between. That's what makes batch-one work viable instead of a headache.

### 5-axis rigidity

Accuracy comes from how the frame damps, not from the brochure. Mid-range machines run around 8,500 kg — about double an entry frame. A light frame won't hold tolerance through a real composite cut.

### Stone is its own job

Sealed rails, heavy guides, spindle cooling. Before buying, confirm it's a stone machine and not a wood router with a stone bit bolted on.

### Laser cutting numbers

±0.03 mm positioning, ±0.02 mm repeat, Ra ≤ 12.5 µm so most parts skip polishing. Sheet-to-tube swap in 5-10 minutes. Full enclosure is what passes EU CE/FDA.

### Sheet-and-tube trade-off

Right call when sheet is the main work and tube is secondary. If tube volume is high, run a flatbed plus a dedicated tube cutter as two lines and roughly double capacity.

### What's inside the machine

MAX / Raycus / IPG sources, RAYTOOLS heads, Leadshine servos, Taiwan rails and racks (OEM to ROCTECH spec), Schneider electrics, S&A chillers. Named brands, not mystery parts.

Sources: roc-tech.com product pages + the 12 customer cases (spec tables and Q&A).

# Sources & Gaps

Where this knowledge base came from, what's solid, and what's still missing.

### What's in here (solid)

• 12 named customer cases — 4 woodworking/plastics, 8 metal lasers, across 12 countries.

• Quantified selling points — accuracy, reliability, material savings, power, compliance.

• The actual shipped laser model map (RCL / RC / ROCLAS).

• Buying / SEO keyword templates.

• Company facts, including the Chinese name (若泰) and certification years.

### What's still missing

• 16 of the 26 official FAQ questions aren't in the local records (only IDs 766-775 captured).

• Accuracy figures disagree: the site lists ±0.05 mm for the RCF1325, the FAQ claims 0.01 mm. Confirm per model before quoting.

• Q&A.doc (old binary format) wasn't parsed. The 10 long English articles were skimmed for structure, not fully absorbed.

• Forum and Reddit customer chatter (humor_faqs, forum_posts) wasn't folded in.

### Where the data came from

**A.** roc-tech.com — about-us, faq, product centre, newslist/1108·1109·1110, contact-us.

**B.** Local 若泰机器资料/案例文件_整理 — 12 case folders (EN docs + photos/video).

**C.** Local — roctech_faqs, CNC路由器采购关键词汇总.xlsx, roctech_10_articles.

Heads-up: laser power, price, and scrap rates are indicative from cases/articles. Quote from ROCTECH directly.

**Note on the brand split:** ROCTECH is the parent (Jinan Ruotai / 若泰). The laser line runs under the ROCLAS name. Both show up in the cases — the Irish shop, for example, crossed from ROCTECH woodworking machines to a ROCLAS laser.

This page is the audit trail. If something here looks off, check it against the source listed before you put it in front of a customer.

## A 2017 ROCTECH RC1530S-ATC Still Running at a Nevada Makerspace

Woodworking · installed 2017

`Woodworking` `Makerspace` `Shared equipment`

**Customer**: The Generator Community Maker Space, Reno, Nevada, USA

**Machine**: ROCTECH RC1530S-ATC wood CNC router with ATC

**Installed**: 2017

**Materials**: Solid wood, plywood, MDF and other panels

### The customer

The Generator is a community makerspace in Reno, Nevada. It bought an RC1530S-ATC automatic-tool-change wood CNC router back in 2017, and the machine has been in near-constant use ever since.

### How the machine is used

Because it is a shared public space, the router is operated by many different people every day. It cuts solid wood, plywood, MDF and other panel materials for maker prototypes, custom furniture, sign engraving and general wood fabrication all year round.

Even after years of heavy-duty operation, the router still runs smoothly and holds stable cutting precision. For a machine that has passed through many hands in a public shop, that says a lot about how it was built.

### Key advantages

  * Proven under heavy shared use: many operators, varied jobs and years of continuous running.
  * A durable structure: delivered in 2017 and still holding its rigidity and machining accuracy.
  * ATC automatic tool changer with a vacuum table, for cutting, grooving, routing and engraving.

### Photos from the customer

![usa-reno customer photo 2](images/usa-reno/2.png) Customer photo 2 of 4
![usa-reno customer photo 3](images/usa-reno/3.png) Customer photo 3 of 4
![usa-reno customer photo 4](images/usa-reno/4.png) Customer photo 4 of 4

**ROCTECH note**

ROCTECH built this machine to survive a public makerspace — handed from one stranger to the next, every day, for years. That's the kind of abuse most shop machines never see, and it's still holding tolerance. If a ROCTECH router can take that, a paid operator's shop is easy.

## Ten Years On: A Romanian Workshop Still Cutting with ROCTECH

Woodworking · 10 years

`Woodworking` `Durability proof`

**Customer**: Woodworking workshop, Romania

**First purchase**: 2016

**Still running**: 10 years and counting

### The customer

A customer in Romania bought our woodworking machinery back in 2016. A decade later those same machines are still turning out work.

### What ten years looks like

The range of work is the proof: gothic-style stage backdrops at music festivals, butterfly-cut lattice panels and glowing carved pavilions. Different jobs, different materials, the same machines day after day.

Ten years of daily use. Ten years of performance without drama. That is what we mean when we talk about ROCTECH durability.

**ROCTECH note**

Ten years on the same machines. ROCTECH doesn't make disposable gear — the Romanian shop is still on the original purchase, not on its third replacement. That's the single strongest durability story in this whole knowledge base, and it's a good one to lead with for any woodworking buyer weighing price against lifespan.

## A Trusted Partner in Chile: Guillermo's HDPE Processing Line

## RCL2040-EX-3K Laser Cutter: An Algerian Fabricator Moves Up to a 2 × 4 m Exchange Table

Metal · replaced old laser

`Laser 3000W` `Exchange table` `Enclosed`

**Customer**: Metal fabrication shop, Algeria

**Machine**: RCL2040-EX-3K fully enclosed fibre laser with shuttle table

**Worktable**: 2000 × 4000 mm (5 × 10 ft) blade table

**Laser**: 3000W MAX source, RAYTOOLS BS03K head

**Warranty**: 3 years on the complete machine

### Who the customer is

The customer runs a metalworking shop in Algeria and has spent more than ten years cutting and forming sheet metal for local industrial buyers. Most of the workload is carbon steel and stainless plate, and as project volumes grew, the limits of the old equipment started showing up in delivery dates and rework.

### What was slowing them down

  * The old 3-axis laser needed manual loading. Someone had to walk every sheet onto the bed, which pushed up labour cost and stretched the processing cycle.
  * Cut quality had dropped. Edges carried heavy slag, dimensions drifted, and seams never quite lined up, so a lot of parts went back for rework.
  * Speed was the biggest problem. Large orders piled up because the machine simply could not keep pace with the shop's growth.

### What we recommended

We put forward the RCL2040-EX-3K. The shuttle table and the enclosure were the two features that mattered most here.

  * 2000 × 4000 mm interchangeable blade table. A full-size sheet is loaded once, and loading and unloading overlap, so the laser spends its time cutting instead of waiting for material.
  * 3000W MAX source with a RAYTOOLS BS03K head. Edges come out clean and burr-free, well ahead of what their old plasma and laser lines could manage.
  * Fully enclosed body, an S&A 3000W chiller and automatic lubrication. It is built for a hot, dusty production floor.
  * Schneider electrical components throughout and a RAYTOOLS control system, backed by a 3-year machine warranty.

### Key specifications

Model| RCL2040-3K
---|---
Working size| 2000 × 4000 mm (5 × 10 ft)
Working table| Blade table
Laser power| 3K-12K
Laser source| MAX
Laser head| RAYTOOLS
Control system| RAYTOOLS
Max rapid travel| 80,000 mm/min
X/Y axis position accuracy| ±0.03 mm / 1000 mm
Working environment| 0-40 °C, humidity ≤ 80%, no condensation
Working voltage| 220V / 380V, 60/50 Hz, 3PH
Auxiliary gas| Air, oxygen, nitrogen
Water chiller| S&A
Packing size| 9000 × 2250 × 2300 mm
Gross / net weight| 3500 kg / 3250 kg

### Questions the customer asked

**Q: Can it cut copper and aluminium, or do the reflective surfaces cause trouble?**
It handles them. The high-reflectivity suppression module takes 1-2 mm copper and 2-3 mm aluminium without a problem.

**Q: Do we need a dedicated room for it?**
No. A 380V supply and reasonable ventilation are enough, because the smoke extraction is built into the machine.

**Q: Can we program offline?**
Yes. The layout can be prepared on a computer first and sent over later, so the machine is not sitting idle while someone draws the next job.

### A smaller alternative

For a shop that only needs a 3000 × 1500 mm working area, the open-type RCL3015-3K covers the same 3000W cutting work without the enclosure or exchange table.

## 3015 Sheet-and-Tube Fibre Laser for a UK Metal Processing Plant

Metal · controlled cost

`Laser 3000W` `Sheet-and-tube`

**Country**: UK

**Work**: Metal sheet and tube cutting

**Machine**: 3015 integrated sheet-and-tube fibre laser, 3000W

**The ask**: One machine, controlled equipment cost

### The situation

The plant processes both sheet and tube but had a limited budget, and a one-time purchase of two separate machines would have put too much pressure on the finances. The practical answer was a single machine that does both.

### What we recommended

A 3015 sheet-and-tube fibre laser at 3000W.

  * One unit replaces a flatbed and a tube cutter, which cuts the procurement cost significantly.
  * It frees up factory floor space compared with two machines.
  * Sheet and tube are handled in the same machine, so there is no cross-machine handling.
  * If tube orders grow later, a dedicated tube cutter can be added without throwing this machine away.

### Technical specifications

  * Cutting area: 1500 × 3000 mm
  * Laser brand: MAX MFSC series, Raycus or IPG
  * Cutting speed: 0-40,000 mm/min
  * Cooling: water cooling
  * Drive: Leadshine servo motors
  * Control: CypCut
  * Laser power: 3000W
  * Supported formats: AI, BMP, Dst, Dwg, DXF, DXP, PLT
  * Materials: various metals

### Questions the customer asked

**Q: What is the machine structure?**
It uses a split-type bed. Production and assembly are controlled so the bed stays parallel, which protects long-term cutting accuracy.

**Q: How do we maintain the chiller?**
Replace the internal circulating water every three months.

**Q: What control system does the fibre laser use?**
The Raytools X3S.

**Q: How many motors drive the tube-cutting tailstock?**
Two.

**Q: Does the machine have CE certification?**
Yes.

### Related machines

For sheet-only work, the RCL3015 flatbed is the simpler choice; for high tube volumes, a dedicated laser tube cutting machine is the way to go.

**ROCTECH note**

One ROCTECH machine did the job of two. The UK plant didn't have the budget for a flatbed and a tube cutter, so ROCTECH put both in one bed — lower spend, less floor, no cross-machine handling. Simple math, lower risk. That's the pitch for any shop that cuts both but doesn't want two machines sitting idle.

🇷🇺

## One Machine for Sheet and Tube: A Russian Craft-Metal Workshop's 3015 Laser

Craft metal · -10 °C

`Laser 3000W` `Sheet-and-tube` `Low temperature`

**Customer**: Metal crafts manufacturer, Russia

**What they make**: Decorative ornaments, openwork pendants, tube-based components

**Machine**: 3015 integrated sheet-and-tube fibre laser, 3000W

**Working environment**: Runs down to -10 °C, built for Russian winters

### The customer and the job

This is a craft metal shop: ornaments, openwork pendants and tube-based parts. Orders come in small batches with a lot of different designs, and the shop pays Russian rent and winter heating on every square metre. Buying two separate machines was never going to make sense.

### Why two machines did not fit

  * A separate flatbed plus a separate tube cutter eats double floor space, and in Russia that means paying for rent and heating twice.
  * Two machines mean two purchase prices, two freight and customs bills, and two sets of spare parts to keep in stock.
  * Moving sheet and tube between two machines adds handling time to every small custom order.
  * Two machines need two operators, and skilled metal workers in Russia are not cheap.
  * Switching between plate and tube work on separate machines is slow when almost every order is a different design.

### What we recommended

A 3015 sheet-and-tube fibre laser at 3000W. One bed, one control, one operator.

  * Cuts plate, round tube and square or rectangular tube on the same machine, so the shop only buys once.
  * Cuts the floor footprint roughly in half, which matters every winter.
  * Uses the same laser system for both materials, so sheet and tube parts line up properly at assembly.
  * Switches between plate and pipe in about five to ten minutes, with no dismantling.
  * Runs in workshops down to -10 °C, with the electrical and optical systems protected for low-temperature work.

### Core specifications

  * Laser power: 3000W (2000W and 3000W available; 3000W recommended for craft work)
  * Plate working area: 3000 × 1500 mm
  * Tube range: round 20-160 mm diameter; square and rectangular 20 × 20 to 120 × 120 mm
  * Cutting accuracy: ±0.03 mm, kerf ≤ 0.1 mm
  * Max plate cut: carbon steel 10 mm, stainless steel 6 mm, aluminium 3 mm
  * Max tube cut: carbon steel 6 mm, stainless steel 4 mm
  * Control: dedicated sheet-and-tube CNC with a built-in craft image library, DXF/DWG import
  * Drive: full servo motors
  * Footprint: about 4.2 m × 2.2 m

### Questions the customer asked

**Q: What metals will it cut?**
Stainless steel, carbon steel, galvanized sheet, aluminium sheet, decorative copper tube and iron tube, which covers the common raw materials used in metal crafts.

**Q: How does the machine get to Russia, and what about customs?**
It ships in a thickened, moisture-proof wooden crate for sea or land transport. We also provide export documents and a certificate of origin to help with Russian customs clearance.

**Q: Will it fail in cold weather?**
The electrical system and laser are treated for low-temperature operation and run stably down to -10 °C. In winter the shop only needs basic insulation.

**Q: Is switching between sheet and pipe a hassle?**
No parts need to be dismantled. The system switches modes with one click, and the pipe fixtures come off quickly. A full switch takes about five to ten minutes.

**Q: Are spare parts available in Russia?**
Common consumables such as lenses, nozzles and ceramic rings ship in bulk with the machine, and we support international express delivery plus video-guided repair for urgent faults.

**Q: Do the cut pieces need grinding afterwards?**
Thin craft sheet comes off essentially burr-free and can go straight to bending or welding, so grinding is mostly eliminated.

**Q: Can we import our own drawing files?**
Yes. The CNC takes DXF and DWG files, so customer-designed ornaments and pipe shapes can be imported and cut directly.

**Q: How hard is it for workers with no experience to learn?**
The interface is in English and comes with tutorials and video training. A new operator can handle plate and pipe programming on their own in two to three days.

### Other machines for similar work

  * Standalone 3015 flatbed fibre laser, for a shop that later turns out to have very little pipe work.
  * Fully automatic tube laser, for a shop whose main business becomes railings and decorative pipe parts.
  * Small 20-100W desktop marking machine, for miniature metal crafts and jewellery-size work.

**ROCTECH note**

ROCTECH sized the machine to Russian winters and Russian rents. The shop lives on small custom orders, so two machines meant double rent, double heating, double operators — ROCTECH put it all in one bed that still runs at -10 °C. When a customer's real constraint is floor space and heating bills, this is the argument that closes: half the footprint, one operator, no dismantling to switch jobs.

## RCL3015-3000W: How a Malaysian Elevator Fabricator Left Plasma Behind

Elevator · dropped plasma

`Laser 3000W` `Replaced plasma` `Higher output`

**Customer**: Tony, elevator sheet-metal factory, Malaysia

**Machine**: RCL3015-3000W fibre laser

**Work**: Elevator car panels, door frames, brackets, stainless decorative parts

**Materials**: 304 stainless 1-6 mm, carbon steel 2-10 mm, aluminium 1-4 mm

**Budget**: RMB 220,000 - 280,000

### The customer and the workload

Tony runs a mid-size elevator component factory in Malaysia. The shop cuts AISI 304 stainless, carbon steel and some aluminium into car panels, door frames, brackets and decorative pattern parts. Peak season comes hard, and the old plasma setup had become the bottleneck.

### Where plasma was costing them

  * Edges came out rough with heavy slag, so every part was hand-polished. Fine holes and small patterns were hit or miss.
  * Aluminium slagged badly and stainless blackened at the cut, so a lot of decorative work was being outsourced and eating into margin.
  * With all the hand finishing, one plasma cutter managed about 30 sets of parts a day. Peak orders meant late deliveries and lost customers.
  * Thermal distortion on shaped parts ran 0.3-0.5 mm off, assembly gaps did not close, and scrap stayed above 8%.
  * Electrodes and nozzles wore out fast, and the noise and smoke were becoming a workshop problem.

### What we recommended

The RCL3015-3000W. The 3000W source matches their material range without paying for power the shop would never use.

  * 3000W cuts 10 mm carbon steel, 6 mm stainless and 4 mm aluminium cleanly, covering the full thickness range they process.
  * Positioning accuracy of ±0.03 mm, repeat accuracy of ±0.02 mm and a minimum kerf of 0.15 mm bring the surface roughness to Ra ≤ 12.5 µm and remove about 80% of the polishing work.
  * The standard 3015 table takes 3 m × 1.5 m sheets, the common size in elevator work, with no custom oversize table needed.
  * 120 m/min rapid travel and 1.5G acceleration cut thin sheet about three times faster than plasma, pushing daily output past 80 sets.

### Questions the customer asked

**Q: Can the 3000W cut 6 mm stainless with a smooth finish?**
Yes. With high-pressure oxygen assist there is no slag adhesion, and Ra stays within 12.5 µm, so decorative panels need no secondary polishing.

**Q: Will it break down running ten hours a day?**
The laser source has a one-year warranty, the head and servo motors are first-tier brands, and the bed is stress-relief annealed. With normal maintenance it runs ten hours a day with under four hours of maintenance downtime a month.

**Q: How much labour does it save compared with plasma?**
Plasma parts currently need five to ten minutes of hand polishing each. The laser removes 70-80% of that, worth two or three polishers a month.

**Q: What comes with the machine, and what are the running consumables?**
It ships with a cutting head, several nozzle sizes, protective lenses, air lines and a tool kit. Regular consumables run about 300-500 Malaysian Ringgit a month, far below plasma electrode and nozzle spend.

**Q: How much floor space does it need?**
The machine is 4.6 m × 2.45 m, needs about 0.8 m of clearance around it, and takes roughly 18 square metres in total. It fits the existing workshop without expansion.

### Related machines

  * Laser cutter with exchange worktables, for shops that want to cut and load at the same time.
  * 6000W high-power fibre laser, for thicker plate.
  * Integrated sheet-and-tube laser, if the shop later adds pipe work.

**ROCTECH note**

Tony dropped plasma for a ROCTECH laser and cut his polishing nearly to zero — about 80% of the hand-finishing gone, daily output past 80 sets. That's the headline for any shop still running plasma: the ROCTECH laser pays for the polishing labour it removes, and the scrap and distortion problems disappear with it. The numbers above are the case, not the pitch.

A 6000W fibre laser. At that power, medium and thick plate moves quickly, and thin sheet runs at high speed.

  * Raytools cutting head and CypCut control system.
  * 1500 × 3000 mm working area, with other sizes available.

## RC3015T-3000W: Sheet and Tube in One Machine for a Spanish Fabricator

Steel structure · replaced two

`Laser 3000W` `Sheet-and-tube` `CE`

**Country**: Spain

**Industry**: Metal and steel-structure fabrication

**Machine**: RC3015T-3000W combined sheet-and-tube fibre laser

**Supplies**: Construction, fitness equipment, agricultural machinery makers

### The customer and the job

The shop works out of a single-storey building and cuts flat sheet and tube at the same time. The finished parts go to local makers in construction, fitness equipment and agricultural machinery, and sheet and tube are often blanked together in one batch.

### What the two-machine setup was costing

  * They already owned a flatbed laser and a plasma tube cutter. Two machines meant double floor space, double procurement and double maintenance, and the tube cutter sat idle whenever tube orders dropped.
  * Moving sheet and tube between two machines stretched out every batch and made rush orders impossible.
  * The old equipment burned edges on stainless and thin plate, so that work went outside, came back slow and raised external processing cost.
  * Two control systems and two spare-parts shelves made fault finding slower, and plasma electrodes and nozzles wore out every month.

### What we recommended

The RC3015T-3000W. One machine does both jobs and does them on the same bed.

  * Integrated sheet and tube processing replaces two machines, cuts floor occupancy by half and lowers the initial investment.
  * The 3000W MAX source cuts 16 mm carbon steel, 8 mm stainless and 6 mm aluminium, covering every conventional thickness in their orders.
  * Repeat positioning of ±0.02 mm, with holes and intersecting tube cuts formed in one pass, cutting polishing labour by about 70%.
  * CE certified with a wide-voltage 3-phase 380V/50Hz input that stays stable within ±10% grid fluctuation, matching Spanish factory power.
  * MAX source, Raytools head and Leadshine servos, with standard spare parts stocked in European warehouses; consumable cost drops about 60% against plasma.

### Key specifications

Laser power| 3000W MAX fibre laser source
---|---
Sheet working size| 3000 × 1500 mm
Tube processing length| 6 m standard, round and square tube
Materials| Carbon steel, stainless steel, galvanized sheet, aluminium alloy
Positioning accuracy| ±0.03 mm
Repeat positioning accuracy| ±0.02 mm
Drive| Leadshine servo motors, dual rack and pinion
CNC system| Raytools intelligent cutting system, DXF and AI import
Cutting head| Raytools auto-focus
Power supply| 3-phase AC 380V / 50Hz
Tube clamping| Front and rear dual pneumatic self-centring chucks

### Questions the customer asked

**Q: Can it cut sheet and tube at the same time?**
No, it is a switchable all-in-one machine. The tube chuck retracts during sheet cutting. It suits a factory where sheet is the main work and tube is secondary, without buying two machines.

**Q: Can the 6 m tube length be extended?**
The standard model takes 6 m tubes, and 3 m or 9 m custom tube racks are available for long structural work.

**Q: Does it come with CE documents, and will customs be a problem?**
Complete CE and RoHS certificates are supplied with English documents and machine nameplates, so the machine clears Spanish ports and can be filed locally without issue.

**Q: What consumables does it need, and can they be bought in Spain?**
Nozzles, protective lenses, coolant and fibre laser protective sleeves. They are standard parts available at local laser accessory suppliers, or we ship a bulk set with the machine.

**Q: Can it cut special-shaped tubes?**
Yes, but that requires a system modification.

### A two-line alternative

For a factory running balanced sheet and tube volumes in parallel, the split setup of an RCL3015-3000W flatbed plus an RCL2400-3000W tube cutter runs both lines at once and roughly doubles total capacity.

**ROCTECH note**

ROCTECH replaced two machines, halved the footprint, and cut polishing 70% — and the CE paperwork cleared Spanish customs without a fight. That combination is the whole sell for European fabricators: one machine instead of two, consumables down ~60% vs plasma, and the certifications (CE, RoHS, English docs) handled up front. When a Spanish shop asks "will this pass customs and inspection?" the answer is in the spec table above.

## RCL3015-3000W with Cover and Push-Pull Table: An Italian Sheet-Metal Shop

Industrial / architectural · EU compliance

`Laser 3000W` `Full enclosure` `FDA / CE`

**Country**: Italy

**Industry**: Sheet-metal fabrication, industrial and architectural

**Work**: 1-12 mm stainless for furniture parts and enclosure panels

**Machine**: RCL3015-3000W, full cover, push-pull table

### The customer and the problems

The shop cuts stainless from 1 mm up to 12 mm into custom furniture components and industrial enclosure panels. Three issues were holding it back.

  * The plasma cutter was too slow on 3-6 mm stainless, which sat right in the middle of their work.
  * Cut quality was inconsistent, with dross and jagged edges that meant heavy secondary finishing.
  * The labour inspectorate had flagged the open machine for not meeting EU CE and FDA safety expectations, and fines were a real risk.
  * New operators kept misplacing the cutting start point and wasting the first sheet of the day.
  * The old generic servos and rails broke down often and delayed deliveries to a key automotive customer.

### What we recommended

The RCL3015-3000W with a full cover and push-pull table.

  * A 3000W Raytools source cuts 0-12 mm stainless about three times faster than plasma, with a nitrogen-assisted oxide-free edge.
  * The 3000 × 1500 mm travel matches standard EU sheet sizes exactly, so sheets go straight on without extra shearing.
  * The full enclosure and FDA/CE compliance clear the Italian labour inspection and protect the operators.
  * The Raytools control panel with a border preview lets operators check the cutting path before starting, so the first sheet is not wasted.
  * Shimpo reducers, Taiwan helical rack and rails, and Schneider electrics keep the machine running through continuous shifts.

### Key specifications

Model| RCL3015-3000W, cover and push-pull table
---|---
Travel size| 3000 × 1500 mm
Laser source| 3000W Max fibre laser, Raytools
Laser head| Raytools auto-focus
Control system| Raytools CNC controller
Drive| Leadshine servo drive, Shimpo reducer
Guide rails| Taiwan square rails, helical rack and pinion, OEM for ROCTECH
Electrical| Schneider (France)
Cooling| S&A 3000W water chiller
Fume extraction| Integrated blower with hoses
Safety standard| FDA and CE compliant, full enclosure
Max cutting speed| Up to 50 m/min
Positioning accuracy| ±0.03 mm/m

### Questions the customer asked

**Q: Can this machine cut 20 mm stainless steel?**
Yes, with oxygen assist and a slower speed. If cuts above 15 mm are frequent, a 6000W model is the better choice.

**Q: The parameters mention Taiwan rails OEM for Roclas. Are they genuine?**
They are made by the same Taiwanese foundry to ROCTECH specifications and quality control, so performance is identical.

**Q: Does the push-pull table need a special foundation?**
No. The frame is pre-levelled and just sits on a flat industrial concrete floor.

**Q: What happens if the fume extractor fails mid-cut?**
The Raytools control detects the airflow loss and pauses the cut automatically to protect the optics.

**Q: Is the software available in Italian?**
Yes, the Raytools system supports Italian, English and Chinese.

**Q: Do you supply EU-compliant plugs?**
Yes, the machine ships with Schneider components and standard Schuko/CE plug configuration.

**Q: How long does a table swap take?**
About 30 seconds, using the pneumatic locking mechanism.

**Q: What is the power draw at full load?**
Roughly 12-15 kW/h including the chiller and fume extractor.

**Q: Can it cut aluminium?**
Yes, up to 8 mm with nitrogen and a coated protective lens that is included in the kit.

**Q: Why does Italy need FDA compliance?**
The FDA laser-safety glass meets the strictest CE requirements, so the machine passes Italian labour inspections without a problem.

### Lower-cost alternatives

Model| Key difference| Best for
---|---|---
RCL3015-2000W| 2000W, standard cover, no push-pull table| Lower budgets cutting mainly 6 mm stainless and below
RCL3015-3000W Eco| No cover, curtain only, no push-pull table, generic reducer| Lowest upfront cost, night-shift shops with light traffic

**ROCTECH note**

ROCTECH closed three gaps at once for this Italian shop: plasma was too slow, scrap from operator error was costing sheets, and the open machine was a fine waiting to happen. The RCL3015-3000W with full enclosure and FDA/CE glass cleared the labour inspection, the border preview stopped the wasted first sheet, and the build (Shimpo, Schneider, Taiwan rails to ROCTECH spec) held up through continuous shifts. For any EU buyer, that compliance-and-reliability combo is the ROCTECH argument — and it's exactly why the FDA glass matters even in Italy.
